Dossier 2: Cross-dressing criminalized (Section 198), enforced with a documented conviction/fine, no document gender change possible, religious penal code with stoning/whipping (moratorium), police intimidation, no independent human rights orgs. This is severe — trans-specific criminal offence on books with enforcement, plus death-penalty code (moratorium, revocable). Not quite near-certain execution, but severe. Score ~0.10-0.15. Cross-dressing ban enforced, cannot align documents. I'd say 0.12.

Dossier 3: Decriminalized 2023, no LGR (resident gap), protections on sexual orientation, documented Pride with police protection and PM support, but also death threats cancelling 2018 Pride, election hate speech, one trans harassment incident (2016), pervasive stigmatisation, polls relatively friendly. No traveler-facing restrictions documented. Mostly positive with some social hostility. ~0.65-0.70.

Dossier 4: Same-sex legal only from 21 (unequal age of consent — criminal exposure for partners under 21), marriage nullity on gender identity grounds (Article 39 — direct trans-specific legal exposure), government cancelled LGBTQ party, government rejected anti-LGBT violence recommendations (state hostility), 2011 report of violence against transgender sex workers including murder (dated, post-coup), social concealment norm, no LGR documented. Data protection laws protective. State threat-framing partially: rejecting recommendations to combat violence, party cancellation. Article 39 gender identity marriage nullity is trans-specific but resident-facing mostly (visitor unlikely married there... actually could matter if married? Visitor's marriage validity—likely not challenged by registrar at travel). The state's rejection of anti-LGBT violence recommendations plus documented violence (dated 2011) and social hostility. No criminalization of identity per se. ~0.45-0.55. Tier 3-ish societal hostility with thin recourse, plus state tolerance of violence. I'd say 0.48.

Dossier 5: Never criminalized, no discrimination law, state practice to tolerate/ignore unless campaigning or immodest, blocked LGBTI webpages, social media crackdown, only one advocacy group, trans visible mainly as entertainment, traditional third-gender presence at temples (transgender people wearing traditional costumes — acceptance signal), diplomatic backing for IDAHOBIT, Pride held. No documented targeting or violence. Open questions on documents. Tolerant-unless-visible state posture. ~0.65-0.70. The state tolerance unless campaigning is a mild caution. Traditional costume visibility positive. No criminalization. I'd say 0.68.

Comparing 1, 3, 5: Dossier 1 has constitutional equality (2018) on sexual orientation, no criminalization, thin otherwise, dated stigma. Dossier 3 has decriminalization + protections + working institutions + documented acceptance but also documented hostility incidents and no LGR. Dossier 5 no criminalization, no discrimination law, state tolerance/ignore, traditional acceptance, but thin and social media repression.

Dossier 3 probably highest given documented Pride, police protection, PM support, polls. Dossier 1 next — clean, no documented negatives, constitutional equality but thin and open questions. Dossier 5 similar to 1 but with state repression signals (blocking LGBTI webpages, immodest-campaigning trigger) — slightly lower.

Set: 1: 0.72, 3: 0.70, 5: 0.66, 4: 0.47, 2: 0.12.

Dossier 1 is clean but thin with open questions. Rule 3: documented positives count. Dossier 3's documented positives are strong; negatives are dated/limited. I'd put 3 slightly above 1: 3: 0.72, 1: 0.70.

Actually dossier 1's constitutional equality reform is a documented positive too. Both around 0.70-0.73. I'll do 1: 0.71, 3: 0.73, 5: 0.66.
